name: AD811 (Analog Devices single high-speed current-feedback op-amp, used as a DAC I/V stage)
tagline: Analog Devices current-feedback video amp (2500 V/us, 25 ns settling) that diyAudio builders use as a very fast I/V stage for current-output DACs.
technology: Single-channel bipolar wideband current-feedback op-amp, designed for broadcast video. Rated 2500 V/us slew, 25 ns settling to 0.1%, 1.9 nV/rtHz voltage noise and ±4.5 V to ±18 V supplies.

part_numbers.status: unknown (product-page lifecycle status not confirmed in this pass)
part_numbers.notes: Base part number; single current-feedback amplifier.
PDIP-8 (ADI 'N' suffix). DigiKey lists it as Obsolete / no longer manufactured. Some DIP units sold for DAC op-amp rolling may be old stock.
RoHS ('Z') PDIP version; radiolocman has a datasheet listing for it. Lifecycle status not confirmed.
SOIC ('R' suffix), J (commercial) grade. Octopart hosts the Rev. E datasheet under this PN. Exact package pin count and status not confirmed.
16-lead wide SOIC, RoHS; RS lists it as a 2500 V/us video amplifier IC in 16-pin SOIC W.
7-inch tape-and-reel version of AD811ARZ-16; radiolocman has a datasheet listing for it.

lineage.period: pre-2004 to present (introduction date unconfirmed; the datasheet went from Rev. D to Rev. E in 7/04 and is now at Rev. G)
lineage.notes: No second sources found. Old datasheet copies carry the 1990s ADI 'a' logo header.

reputation.summary: diyAudio posters rate it highly as an I/V converter for current-output DACs. There is a dedicated thread ('AD811 as I/V stage for current DACs...'), a build thread ('AD811 IV completed and tested') and posts in the long 'Best opamp for I/V conversion?' thread. Those posters say it sounds better than other op-amps they tried in a classic I/V stage, including an OPA861 alternative. They credit its 2500 V/us slew and 25 ns settling (versus about 550 ns quoted for the OPA627). This is enthusiast forum opinion, not measured audio data.
typical_uses: I/V converter after current-output audio DACs (posters mention PCM61, PCM1702 and similar)
caveats: Current-feedback amplifier: the feedback resistor value sets bandwidth and stability. The usual voltage-feedback I/V topology with a capacitor directly across the feedback resistor needs care with a CFA.
Runs hot: diyAudio posters recommend a small heatsink at ±14 V supplies.
AD811AN (DIP-8) is listed obsolete at DigiKey. Newer stock is SOIC (including the 16-lead wide SOIC AD811ARZ-16), so DIP sockets need an adapter.
The praise comes from a handful of diyAudio threads. It is subjective, and treating slew rate or settling time as proof of sound quality is the posters' reasoning, not ADI's.

counterfeit_notes: No AD811-specific counterfeit reports were found in this pass. AD811AN (PDIP-8) is listed obsolete at DigiKey, so DIP-8 AD811s sold cheaply on marketplaces for DAC op-amp rolling are old stock at best and may be relabelled. Check date codes and markings, and check that the part shows current-feedback behaviour and very fast edges.
alternatives: OPA861 (compared against the AD811 in the diyAudio I/V thread)
AD844 (another ADI current-feedback amp often used for DAC I/V)
OPA627 (voltage-feedback I/V favourite; diyAudio posters contrast its 550 ns settling)

claims_confirmed: The current ADI AD811 datasheet is Rev. G at analog.com, also indexed as 'AD811 (Rev. G)' at the legacy path: https://www.analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets/AD811.pdf
A radiolocman copy is labelled 'Revision: G', with ADI quick links reading 'Last Content Update: 02/23/2017': https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=121471&p=1
The Rev. E datasheet is mirrored at Mouser: https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/609/AD811-256255.pdf
The Rev. E datasheet is mirrored at Octopart under AD811JR: https://datasheet.octopart.com/AD811JR-Analog-Devices-datasheet-87460.pdf
Rev. D to Rev. E (7/04) changes were: updated format, Maximum Power Dissipation section, Ordering Guide and Outline Dimensions: https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/609/AD811-256255.pdf
A Rev. F copy exists on studylib: https://studylib.net/doc/18789058/ad811--rev.-f-

Specs: 140 MHz (G=+1) and 120 MHz (G=+2) -3 dB bandwidth; 35 MHz 0.1 dB bandwidth; 2500 V/us slew; 25 ns settling to 0.1% (2 V step) and 65 ns to 0.01% (10 V step); 1.9 nV/rtHz noise; 0.01%/0.01° DG/DP; ±4.5 V to ±18 V supplies; ±2.3 V into 75 Ω at ±5 V: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD811.pdf
AD811ARZ-16 is a 16-pin wide-SOIC 2500 V/us video amplifier listed at RS: https://nz.rs-online.com/web/p/video-amplifiers-ics/5237689
